# References

Primary literature, documentation, and data sources consulted in the preparation of this textbook. All U.S.-based sources.

1. Anselin, L. (1995). Local indicators of spatial association—LISA. Geographical Analysis, 27(2), 93–115.

2. Anselin, L. (1988). Spatial Econometrics: Methods and Models. Dordrecht: Kluwer Academic Publishers.

3. Brunsdon, C., Fotheringham, A.S., & Charlton, M.E. (1996). Geographically weighted regression: a method for exploring spatial nonstationarity. Geographical Analysis, 28(4), 281–298.

4. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. CDC WONDER: Wide-ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research. wonder.cdc.gov. Accessed 2026.

5. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry. (2022). CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index. Atlanta, GA: CDC.

6. Drez, D.N., et al. (2023). Rural-urban disparities in health outcomes, clinical care, health behaviors, and social determinants of health. PLOS Global Public Health, 3(10), e0002420.

7. Federal Office of Rural Health Policy (FORHP). (2025). How We Define Rural. Health Resources and Services Administration. hrsa.gov/rural-health/about-us/what-is-rural.

8. Federal Office of Rural Health Policy. (2025). FORHP Eligible Areas Data Files. hrsa.gov/rural-health/about-us/what-is-rural/data-files. September 2025 update using 2025 RUCA and RRS data.

9. Health Resources and Services Administration. Area Health Resources Files (AHRF). data.hrsa.gov/topics/health-workforce/nchwa/ahrf. Accessed 2026.

10. Health Resources and Services Administration. Health Professional Shortage Area (HPSA) Data Files. data.hrsa.gov. Accessed 2026.

11. JuliaGeo Organization. JuliaGeo: Geospatial Computing in Julia. juliageo.org. GitHub: github.com/JuliaGeo. Accessed 2026.

12. Hoffimann, J. et al. Geospatial Data Science with Julia. juliaearth.github.io/geospatial-data-science-with-julia. Open source textbook, JuliaEarth organization.

13. Luo, W., & Wang, F. (2003). Measures of spatial accessibility to health care in a GIS environment: synthesis and a case study in the Chicago region. Environment and Planning B, 30(6), 865–884.

14. Moran, P.A.P. (1950). Notes on continuous stochastic phenomena. Biometrika, 37(1-2), 17–23.

15. National Center for Health Statistics. National Vital Statistics System. cdc.gov/nchs/nvss. Accessed 2026.

16. Rekow, L., et al. (2025). Geospatial Data Analysis for Identifying and Addressing Health Inequities in Rural America. ResearchGate preprint.

17. Tobler, W. (1970). A computer movie simulating urban growth in the Detroit region. Economic Geography, 46(suppl 1), 234–240.

18. U.S. Census Bureau. TIGER/Line Shapefiles. census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/tiger-line-file.html. Accessed 2026.

19. USDA Economic Research Service. Rural-Urban Commuting Area (RUCA) Codes. ers.usda.gov/data-products/rural-urban-commuting-area-codes. Updated 2025.

20. USDA Economic Research Service. Rural-Urban Continuum Codes (Beale Codes). ers.usda.gov/data-products/rural-urban-continuum-codes. Accessed 2026.

21. Wang, F. (2015). Quantitative Methods and Socioeconomic Applications in GIS (2nd ed.). CRC Press.

22. Weeks, W.B., et al. (2023). Rural-urban disparities in health outcomes, clinical care, health behaviors, and social determinants of health and an action-oriented, dynamic tool for visualizing them. PLOS Global Public Health, 3(10), e0002420.
